title: Tiny Derived Value
intent: Turn one or two changing inputs into a smaller derived value, then observe it at the boundary.
public_summary: The smallest useful recipe: explicit input facts, one derived reduction, one boundary observer.

public_sections.heading: Recipe Shape
body: Use this when a UI, process, or integration needs one clear output from a small set of changing inputs.
bullets: Observe the output at the edge.

title: Form Summary
intent: Reduce many field updates into one validation or submission summary.
public_summary: A fan-in recipe for forms, settings panels, and other many-input surfaces.

public_sections.heading: Recipe Shape
body: Each field stays explicit. A derived summary waits for real input according to the package helper and publishes one reduced view for display or submit decisions.
bullets: Keep missing fields honest instead of using fake defaults.
Use a derived summary node for validation.
Let package-local examples provide exact syntax.

title: Event to State
intent: Accept external events at a source boundary and reduce them into graph-visible state.
public_summary: A boundary recipe for turning external event streams into inspectable graph state.

public_sections.heading: Recipe Shape
body: Use a package-owned source or adapter to bring events into the graph. Once inside, model state and projections as normal declared graph material.
bullets: Do not trigger internal work through hidden callbacks.
Keep async/event IO at the source boundary.

title: Terminal Report
intent: Collect or reduce input until completion, then publish a final report.
public_summary: A recipe for imports, batch jobs, final summaries, and bounded streams.

public_sections.heading: Recipe Shape
body: Some outputs are meaningful only after upstream work settles. Keep that lifecycle in the graph instead of polling or reading caches from the side.
bullets: Use terminal-aware package helpers for syntax.
Publish the final result through an effect or package adapter.

title: Boundary IO
intent: Connect files, network, workers, or remote graphs without putting async or hidden runtime behavior in the sync core.
public_summary: A recipe for external systems: adapters at the boundary, declared facts inside the graph.

public_sections.heading: Recipe Shape
body: The shared site describes the boundary discipline. Concrete IO helpers, worker integration, bridge setup, and runnable examples remain package-local.
bullets: Keep async work in sources, pools, or bridges.
Re-enter the graph through explicit facts.
Use package docs for environment-specific APIs.
